headline.headline: RAYS DEMOLISH ROYALS, 13-2, AS CAMINERO BLASTS No. 19
headline.deck: Tampa Bay erupts for five runs in the eighth to turn a rout into a blowout
headline.body:
ST. PETERSBURG — Junior Caminero crushed his 19th home run of the season and the Tampa Bay Rays sent the Kansas City Royals home embarrassed Thursday night, piling up 13 runs in a 13-2 shellacking at Tropicana Field before 14,276 fans. The Rays never trailed, scoring twice in the first inning before adding three in the fourth, two in the fifth and — in case any doubt lingered — five more in the eighth to put the game well beyond reach.

Kansas City managed nothing through eight full innings before scratching out a pair of runs in the ninth against Tampa Bay's relievers. By then the damage was done. Jensen launched homer No. 11 on the night, Caminero added his 19th, and a third player identified in the scoring summary as Jr. chipped in his third of the year. Díaz and Aranda each added doubles as the Rays offense worked methodically through a Royals pitching staff that had no answers.

The game was completed in a brisk 2 hours and 19 minutes, which was perhaps a mercy for the visitors. Kansas City, sitting at fourth in the AL West entering Thursday, got only those two consolation runs in the ninth to show for a miserable evening in Florida. Tampa Bay, meanwhile, sent a loud message that their lineup can erupt at any moment — and that an eight-run lead is still not safe from further punishment.

secondary.headline: ATHLETICS RALLY IN NINTH FOR 9-6 WIN OVER GIANTS
secondary.deck: Oakland scores four in the ninth to escape San Francisco with a road victory
secondary.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Athletics were in serious trouble when the Giants erupted for five runs in the sixth inning to take a 6-2 lead at Oracle Park on Thursday evening. It looked like a blown opportunity for Oakland. Then came the ninth. The Athletics pushed across four runs in the final frame to complete a stunning 9-6 comeback victory before 33,089 fans, with Caleb Kilian earning the win.

The A's had scored twice in the fifth before the Giants' sixth-inning burst threatened to blow the game open. Oakland answered with two in the seventh, one in the eighth and then four in the ninth to seal it. Mitch Susac entered as a pinch hitter in the sixth and McNeil was hit by a pitch from Roupp during the contest. The victory keeps the Athletics relevant in the AL West race as the calendar turns toward late June.

secondary.headline: AVALANCHE TRADE NICHUSHKIN TO BLUE JACKETS IN SWEEPING OFFSEASON OVERHAUL
secondary.deck: Colorado continues dramatic roster teardown, shipping veteran winger to Columbus
secondary.body:
DENVER — The Colorado Avalanche traded longtime winger Valeri Nichushkin to the Columbus Blue Jackets on Thursday, the latest move in a sweeping offseason reconstruction that has reshaped the franchise that once won the Stanley Cup. Nichushkin, a physical presence on Colorado's top lines for several seasons, becomes one of the more notable names to change addresses as NHL general managers scramble to reposition their rosters following the conclusion of the playoffs.

The deal signals that Colorado's front office is serious about building a new core rather than clinging to familiar names. Nichushkin had become a complicated figure in Denver after a leave of absence from the team in recent years. NHL trade activity is running at a furious pace this offseason, with multiple contenders retooling and rebuilding franchises hunting for veteran pieces. The Blue Jackets add a recognizable winger as they continue their own slow climb back toward relevance in the Metropolitan Division.

secondary.headline: MARK WILLIAMS AGREES TO RETURN TO SUNS ON THREE-YEAR, $38M DEAL
secondary.deck: Restricted free agent center intends to stay in Phoenix on fully guaranteed contract
secondary.body:
PHOENIX — Restricted free agent center Mark Williams intends to sign a three-year, $38 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Phoenix Suns, sources confirmed Thursday, giving the franchise a dependable big man as NBA free agency shifts into high gear. The deal keeps Williams in the desert after he established himself as a valued piece of the frontcourt rotation this past season.

The signing comes amid a flurry of NBA offseason activity that also includes Austin Reaves agreeing to stay with the Los Angeles Lakers. Williams, still young and with room to develop, gives Phoenix a cost-controlled center at a position where options can be scarce. The Suns have been aggressive in trying to stabilize their roster after a turbulent stretch of seasons, and locking in Williams on a reasonable deal represents exactly the kind of foundational move a front office in transition needs to make.

column.headline: THE RAYS REMINDED EVERYONE: MERCY RULES EXIST FOR A REASON
column.body:
Thirteen runs against two. Five of them arriving in the eighth inning, when the game was already a foregone conclusion. What unfolded Thursday night at Tropicana Field was not a baseball game so much as a formal statement of intent from a Rays lineup that appears to have genuinely lost interest in pitchers who fall behind early. Caminero at 19 home runs before the Fourth of July. Jensen at 11. The Rays are not supposed to be this dangerous, and yet here we are.

The Royals managed to score twice — in the ninth, against mop-up arms, in a game decided hours earlier. That is the kind of footnote that stings in a clubhouse. Kansas City came to Florida and was not merely beaten but systematically dismantled over 2 hours and 19 minutes. Tampa Bay is a franchise built on pitching and defense and smart process. When the lineup catches fire on top of all that, the results look exactly like what we saw Thursday. The rest of the American League has been warned.

story.headline: PHILLIES RALLY FROM 5-0 HOLE TO STUN NATIONALS, 10-5
story.deck: Harper, Marsh, Hill and Mead homer as Philadelphia erases early five-run deficit
story.body:
WASHINGTON, June 25 -- The Philadelphia Phillies trailed by five runs before they had recorded a single out in the top of the first inning, then came all the way back to thrash the Washington Nationals 10-5 Thursday at Nationals Park, capping the comeback with a five-run ninth inning that turned a nervous one-run lead into a rout.

Washington sent four runs across in the bottom of the first and added another in the third to build a 5-0 cushion, but Philadelphia chipped away with two in the sixth and three in the seventh before Harper, who launched his 18th home run of the season, and Marsh, who added his 12th, powered the visitors into the lead. Hill's sixth home run and Mead's 14th provided the knockout blows in the ninth as the Phillies sent 10 men to the plate in the final frame. Marsh and Crews each swiped a base in a night when Philadelphia's offense refused to stay quiet, finishing with 18 runners left on base in a game that lasted 2 hours and 57 minutes before 28,919 fans.

The comeback overshadowed the rest of a busy Thursday slate that included Tampa Bay's 13-2 demolition of Kansas City, with Caminero slamming his 19th home run and the Rays piling on five runs in the eighth, and the Boston Red Sox handing the first-place New York Yankees a 6-3 defeat at Fenway Park behind home runs from Caballero and Durbin. The Red Sox, 15 games behind New York in the AL East, erupted for four runs in the fifth inning to wipe out a 2-0 deficit and have now won the series opener against the Yankees.

story.headline: REAVES STAYS, WILLIAMS RETURNS AS NBA OFFSEASON HITS FULL STRIDE
story.deck: Lakers lock up Reaves while Suns re-sign Williams to anchor frontcourt rebuild.
story.body:
The 2026 NBA free agency period roared to life Friday with a flurry of signings and extensions reshaping rosters across the league. Austin Reaves, the sharpshooting guard who became a fan favorite and legitimate weapon during his tenure with the Los Angeles Lakers, agreed to a new deal to remain in Hollywood, drawing high marks from analysts grading the league's busiest offseason movement. The Lakers, determined to keep their supporting cast intact around their franchise cornerstone, made Reaves a priority from the moment the offseason began.

In Phoenix, the Suns secured one of the more significant restricted free agent decisions of the early period, with center Mark Williams agreeing to return on a three-year, fully guaranteed contract worth $38 million. Williams, whose size and shot-blocking ability gave Phoenix a legitimate interior presence, had drawn interest from around the league, but the Suns exercised their matching rights and kept him in the desert. The deal signals Phoenix's commitment to building around a young frontcourt rather than chasing another splashy veteran trade.

Meanwhile, the Portland Trail Blazers filled their long-vacant head coaching seat with Micah Nori, who revealed Thursday that multiple NBA organizations had informed him he was their second choice before Portland finally came calling. Nori, patient through a lengthy process, said he never got discouraged. On a lighter note, Narcisse Ngoy, selected 57th overall in this week's draft by the Clippers, announced he intends to return to Auburn for another college season rather than turn professional immediately, a rare path for a drafted prospect.

story.headline: AVALANCHE SHIP NICHUSHKIN TO COLUMBUS AS 2026 OFFSEASON RESHUFFLING HITS FULL STRIDE
story.deck: Colorado continues roster overhaul while Florida lands Hathaway to replace departing Greer.
story.body:
The NHL offseason trade market exploded Thursday with Colorado trading winger Valeri Nichushkin to the Columbus Blue Jackets, a stunning move that signals the Avalanche are serious about remaking a roster that fell short of Stanley Cup expectations. Nichushkin, 31, spent years as one of Colorado's most reliable power forwards alongside Nathan MacKinnon and Mikko Rantanen, but general manager Chris MacFarland appears committed to a youth movement as the franchise searches for its next championship window.

Florida Panthers general manager Bill Zito moved swiftly to plug a looming hole on his fourth line, acquiring gritty winger Garnet Hathaway from the Philadelphia Flyers with veteran agitator A.J. Greer expected to bolt in free agency. Hathaway, 34, brings exactly the physical, penalty-killing presence that head coach Paul Maurice prizes in his system, and the defending-contender Panthers made clear they have no intention of softening their identity heading into the 2026-27 season.

Elsewhere on a busy Thursday, PWHL Detroit landed a marquee signing as five-time Olympian Hilary Knight agreed to a two-year contract extension with the expansion franchise, giving the Motor City club an instant face of the program. Meanwhile, Montreal Victoire captain Marie-Philip Poulin revealed she hoisted the Walter Cup while playing through both a torn ACL and a torn meniscus, a disclosure that left the hockey world marveling at the 30-year-old's extraordinary toughness and cementing her status as the sport's defining female competitor.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS NFL OFFSEASON RESHAPES ROSTERS ACROSS THE LEAGUE
story.deck: Big-name signal-callers are on the move as teams retool for 2026.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has produced a dizzying series of quarterback moves that could redraw the league's power structure heading into 2026. The Las Vegas Raiders completed a trade for veteran passer Sam Darnold, sending a second-round pick to Minnesota in exchange for the journeyman starter who showed flashes of elite play during stretches of the 2025 season. Meanwhile, the New Orleans Saints inked former Pittsburgh Steelers backup Kyle Allen to a two-year, $28 million deal, signaling the franchise's intent to compete after a disappointing 7-10 finish last year.

The NFL Draft last month injected fresh talent into struggling franchises, with the Cleveland Browns selecting Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders with the first overall pick. Sanders, whose arm strength and pocket presence drew comparisons to Patrick Mahomes during the pre-draft evaluation process, arrived in Cleveland to immediate fanfare. The Tennessee Titans, drafting second, took Penn State edge rusher Abdul Carter, a decision their defensive coordinator praised as a cornerstone move for a rebuilt front seven.

Training camps remain weeks away, but roster construction is already generating headlines. The Dallas Cowboys released four-time Pro Bowl receiver CeeDee Lamb after contract negotiations collapsed, and Lamb drew immediate interest from the Philadelphia Eagles and San Francisco 49ers. The defending Super Bowl LX champion Kansas City Chiefs, meanwhile, quietly restructured Patrick Mahomes' contract to create cap space, strongly suggesting another major free-agent addition is imminent before July rosters lock in.
